look_here_first: Look for narrow linear leaflets plus a dense swollen cylindrical-to-ovoid head. If the real question is D. compacta versus D. purpurea, move immediately to the calyx.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: few pairs of narrow linear to linear-elliptic leaflets

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: very dense terminal ovoid/oblong/cylindrical flower head

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: D. purpurea separation depends strongly on calyx characters

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Clumping herbaceous perennial from thick root/short caudex.

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: Few pairs of narrow linear to linear-elliptic leaflets; var. pubescens commonly under 3 mm wide.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Very dense swollen ovoid, oblong or cylindrical/conelike head.

key_traits.label: Calyx
key_traits.text: Priority structure for separation from D. purpurea; use size and external pubescence pattern rather than flower color.
